clue.text: Cut down on the jumping; it's going on and on!

parts.note: bound means a leap, so jumping gives this word
to cut down on something is to do less of it

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea to stop all the bouncing about, which seems never to end.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Cut down on the jumping' as an instruction: do less bounding, giving BOUND then LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boundless has no limit, so it seems to continue endlessly.

clue.text: Do live on a wreck!

definitions.note: a do is a party, a noun here

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: to wreck something is to smash it up, so these letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and live aboard a shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like the verb opening a command; it is the noun for a party. A beano is British slang for a lively celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is informal British slang for a party or celebration, as is a do.

clue.text: Playing iTunes on large device

indicators.note: playing about with letters loosens their order, so the brand name is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone running iTunes on an oversized gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iTunes' and 'device' sit together as a tech scene, but the brand name is just raw letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or implement, a practical device for a task, especially in a kitchen.

clue.text: Dutch city was the first to get up a newspaper

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to have led is to have been first
the FT is the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A Dutch city boasts it was the first to set up a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up' suggests founding a paper; in this down clue it reverses LED.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is a city in the Netherlands, famous for its blue-and-white pottery.

clue.text: Fantastic island life — yes, one would be dead blessed here!

definitions.text: one would be dead blessed here
definitions.note: a description of a place, matching the noun phrase answer

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something fanciful or wildly transformed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fantasy of island living so good that the dead would count themselves lucky to be there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead blessed' reads as slang for very lucky; here it means the blessed dead, who in Greek myth went to this paradise.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the Elysian Fields were the paradise where heroes and the virtuous dwelt after death.

clue.text: Uncle's cut off a cactus?

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An uncle has sliced a piece off a cactus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' reads as a single phrase; 'cut' is fodder and 'off' alone signals the rearrangement. The question mark admits a cactus is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A succulent is a plant with thick fleshy water-storing tissue, and the cactus is the best-known example.

clue.text: Gather undoctored author lacks English

definitions.note: to gather here is to infer or work out

indicators.note: lacks means is missing, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Dr Seuss without his title 'Dr' is just Seuss

explanation.surface: Collecting the works of an author who never had a doctorate and lacks an English degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undoctored' plays on Dr Seuss, the children's author: strip the Dr and you have SEUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: To suss something is informal British for to work it out or realise it, as in gather meaning infer.

clue.text: Malicious gossip when Charlie appears in casual wear

indicators.note: appears in means turns up inside, so the letter is placed within the word

parts.note: a sandal is a piece of casual footwear
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Tongues wag when Charlie turns up dressed casually.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is outrage or talk caused by reported wrongdoing, much like spiteful rumour.

clue.text: Shock problem arising from acrobatic manoeuvre over object

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: the splits is a gymnastic move with the legs flat in opposite directions
ends are aims or objects, as in 'means to an end'

explanation.surface: A shocking injury resulting from a gymnast's move over some apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' suggests a fright; it is a shock of hair, a thick mass.
explanation.definitionFit: Split ends are damaged hair tips that fray in two, a common hair complaint.

clue.text: Story of western state with arable land

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
a ley is a field temporarily under grass in arable rotation

explanation.surface: The tale of a western US state full of farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: Waverley is Walter Scott's first novel; 'western state' suggests America but splits into W and AVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Waverley is the 1814 novel by Sir Walter Scott, a work of fiction.

clue.text: Chain reaction starts melting lead protection rocker?

indicators.note: starts means the opening letter of each of these words

parts.note: the first letters of chain and reaction

indicators.note: melting metal loses its shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A nuclear chain reaction gets going, melting the lead shielding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead protection' looks like radiation shielding; the definition is a cradle, which both protects a baby and rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle is a baby's bed that rocks, keeping the infant safe and soothed.

clue.text: Well prepared for means of restraining corporation

definitions.note: corporation is old jocular British slang for a pot belly

parts.note: Cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'well!'
set means ready or prepared, as in 'all set for'

explanation.surface: A firm that is well equipped to keep a business in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a company; it is humorous slang for a large paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is a tight undergarment worn to shape the body and hold in a protruding stomach.

clue.text: One sister needs to go steady with flood

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
a nun is a religious sister
to date someone is to go out with them regularly

explanation.surface: A nun must start seeing someone seriously, and floods follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to swamp or overwhelm with water, the same as to flood.

clue.text: Tip: on board ship, they help one look down on others

definitions.text: they help one look down on others

indicators.note: on board means carried inside, so this word goes within the ship's letters

parts.note: to tip is to tilt

explanation.surface: A piece of advice aboard ship about looking down on fellow passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look down on others' suggests snobbery; it is meant literally, from a raised height. SS stands for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilts raise the wearer high off the ground, so they literally gaze down at people below.

clue.text: Golf club about to be engulfed by the press

indicators.note: engulfed by means swallowed inside, so the short word sits within the others

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A golf club about to be swamped by journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The press' suggests reporters; it is ironing. RE goes into THE, giving THREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-iron is a golf club with a fairly low-lofted metal head, used for long shots.

clue.text: Obstruct a film director with everything

parts.note: Oliver Stone is an American film director
all means everything

explanation.surface: Getting in the way of a movie director who has it all.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to block or delay by refusing to cooperate or answer.

clue.text: Annoying press broadcast on moorland plant

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the airwaves, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: to knead dough is to press it
ling is heather, which covers moorland

explanation.surface: An irritating media report about some heather on the moors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press broadcast' suggests the news media; the press here is the kneading of dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Needling means irritating or provoking someone persistently, as in teasing them.

clue.text: Dozens abroad show disgust

parts.note: a gross is twelve dozen
abroad means out and about, away from home

explanation.surface: Many people overseas display their revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross out is informal for to sicken or revolt, causing a reaction of revulsion.

clue.text: Cloud's position hiding rook

definitions.note: read as 'cloud is', with the 's a link to the wordplay

indicators.note: hiding means concealing inside, so the letter is placed within the word

parts.note: status is standing or position

explanation.surface: A cloud's location conceals a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: R for rook is a chess abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a low, flat, grey type of cloud forming a uniform layer.

clue.text: In fact, her most insulated soup holder?

indicators.note: insulated means wrapped up inside, so the letters lie within these words

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of fact, all of her and the start of most

explanation.surface: A wry remark that a flask is, in fact, the best-insulated thing she owns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insulated' sits naturally with a flask, which disguises its job.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thermos is a vacuum flask that keeps drinks or soup hot; the question mark admits it holds other things too.

clue.text: Within litter, hearts beat

indicators.note: within means placed inside, so the letter sits in the word

parts.note: trash is litter or rubbish

explanation.surface: Among a litter of puppies, hearts are beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearts beat' looks like a tender scene; H for hearts is the card-suit abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash is to hit hard and repeatedly, or to defeat soundly.

clue.text: Woodland dweller's bank, said to have not much money

definitions.note: read as 'woodland dweller is', with the 's a link

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a bank of seats or keys is a row
a buck is a single dollar

explanation.surface: A forest creature's riverbank home is rumoured to be worth little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests a river or money; it is a row, as in a bank of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A roebuck is the male roe deer, which lives in woodland.

clue.text: Recover from unfinished excursion nursed by old official

indicators.note: nursed by means held inside, so the shortened word goes within

parts.note: a reeve was a local magistrate or official in medieval England

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a trip is an excursion

explanation.surface: Getting over a cut-short outing with the help of an old official.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrieve is to get back or regain something lost.

clue.text: See 4
Public meeting wanting tramp beheaded

parts.note: for means in favour of or wanting, as in 'all for it'

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is removed

parts.note: bum is slang for a tramp or vagrant

explanation.surface: A town meeting demanding a vagrant be executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like lacking; it means keen on, giving FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a gathering or venue for open public discussion.

clue.text: Old city captured by the Germanic artist

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so this piece goes within

parts.note: der is the German for 'the'
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient city taken by Germanic tribes.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and engraver.

clue.text: Emblem of South Africa: river within a river with drink

indicators.note: within means placed inside, so the letter sits in the river's name

parts.note: the Po is a river in Italy
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A description of South Africa's national symbol built from rivers and a cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, appearing on its coat of arms and sports badges.

clue.text: Place for those who are no longer represented by mayor — true? Not quite

definitions.text: Place for those who are no longer

indicators.note: represented means presented again in new form, so these letters are rearranged
not quite means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A doubt whether a town's dead are truly represented by their mayor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those who are no longer' looks like former residents; it means the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortuary is a room where dead bodies are kept before burial or cremation.

clue.text: Animals vocalised on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back means travelling in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: something sung has been vocalised

explanation.surface: Animals calling out on their return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus are wildebeest, large African antelopes.

clue.text: Low-cost airline once involving Moss — surprisingly, it's unprofitable

definitions.note: describes a thing, matching the noun answer

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the rearranged name goes inside

parts.note: Laker Airways was Freddie Laker's pioneering cut-price British airline, defunct since 1982

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected arrangement, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An old budget airline signing up Moss, a move that surprisingly loses money.
explanation.walkthrough: Moss could be Kate or Stirling Moss, but the name is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lossmaker is a business or venture that loses money rather than earning it.
